free_text: The patient is a 62-year-old male with a significantly elevated PSA of 160.0 ng/mL and a PI-RADS 5 MRI finding indicating a T3a disease with extracapsular extension. Histology shows Gleason 3+4 (ISUP Grade Group 2). The management assessment requires a clinical review of treatment versus surveillance, balancing the documented extent of the disease against patient preferences.
